page.layout: One page of verse in one column, with a title line in italics set apart; page number and running head at the top; a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Sic communis erat suibus tum sylua Sophisque, Non vno solitis se satiare cibo. Hi sophia mentes, ventres sed glandibus illi Implebant: locus ast vnus virifque fuit. Nil locus ad mores: alioquin pigra propago Porcorum fieret docta corona σφῶν[?].

p.i: Latent maligni rebus aduersis: qui quales sint rebus secundis apparet.

main_text.p: Frigore serpentes nigris conduntur in antris, Noxia sunt & tunc atra venena minus. Aëra sed zephyri dum mulcent, sibila lingua Emittunt, virus lethiferumque vomunt. In rebus latitant duris plerumque maligni, Tempora prodere quos prosperiora solent.

head.i: Quàm sit fœda Idololatria. Ex Eusèb: præp. Euang.lib.6.& Ezechiele 20.

main_text.p: An dici possit, DEVS EST SCARABÆVS (vt olim Ora Sophistarum deblaterasse ferunt) Ostendit Memphis, vocitans quæ solis anœni Hunc animam, stolidè credidit esse Deum. Ostendere pij vates ridere sueti Idola, atque Deos dicere stercoreos. Nascitur in turpi viuens Scarabæus oleto, Cui rosa præsentem gignit odora necem. Sic idolorum qui stercora fœdus honorat, Ferre-nequit, quæ sunt in pietate, rosas. Quòd si sunt similes idolis illa colentes, Dum colit Ægyptus stercora, stercus erit.

page.notes: Marginal fragments at the left and right edges (stains, show-through) are not transcribed. The Greek word at the end of the second stanza is doubtful. The italic title line is set as a heading. Pisc at lower right is taken as the catchword.
